prompt: Match each kind of denial of service to where it is absorbed.

pairs.right: the firewall and the TCP stack
the proxy, the application, a cache

prompt: The office link carries 1 Gbit/s and 20 Gbit/s of flood arrive. What can fw's rules do about it?

choices.text: Drop the flood and keep the good traffic
choices.why: The link is full before fw sees anything.

choices.text: Rate-limit the flood to 1 Gbit/s
choices.why: Rate-limiting happens after the link, too late.

choices.text: Nothing
choices.why: Right. It is lost on the provider's side of the cable.

choices.text: Send a reset to every source
choices.why: That would add traffic, not remove it.

prompt: A link carries 1 Gbit/s and a flood of 20 Gbit/s arrives. How many times the link's capacity is the flood?
A sale e-mailed to a million customers makes the shop unavailable. What does this lesson call that?

choices.text: Not a denial of service, because it is legitimate traffic
choices.why: The effect is the same exhaustion.

choices.text: A denial of service by accident
choices.why: Right. The same exhaustion without an attacker.

choices.text: A distributed denial of service
choices.why: Distributed means many attacking machines.

choices.text: A reflection attack
choices.why: Nothing was reflected.

prompt: When does a server hold a half-open connection?

choices.text: After the client's ACK, before any data
choices.why: After the ACK the connection is open.

choices.text: Between its SYN-ACK and the client's ACK
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: While the connection is closing
choices.why: That is TIME_WAIT and friends.

choices.text: Before the client's SYN arrives
choices.why: There is nothing to hold before the SYN.

prompt: With SYN cookies active and the queue full, what does the server remember about a new SYN?

choices.text: Nothing: it is encoded in the SYN-ACK's sequence number
choices.why: Right. The client's ACK brings it back.

choices.text: The client's address, in a smaller table
choices.why: No table at all.

choices.text: A cookie file in its memory
choices.why: The name is a metaphor.

choices.text: The full SYN, until the ACK arrives
choices.why: That is what happens without cookies.

prompt: How many seconds did fw keep a connection that had seen the SYN-ACK, before the lesson shortened it?
Why does shortening the syn_recv timeout cost legitimate clients nothing?
hint: How long does a real handshake take?

choices.text: Legitimate clients do not use TCP
choices.why: They do.

choices.text: Their entries are marked ASSURED and skip the timeout
choices.why: ASSURED needs traffic both ways, after the handshake.

choices.text: They finish the handshake in milliseconds
choices.why: Right. Only unfinished handshakes wait that long.

choices.text: sysctl -w applies only to new attackers
choices.why: It applies to every entry in that state.

prompt: remote opened six connections under the limit of four. How many were refused?
While remote was at its limit, branch opened a connection to the shop. What happened?
hint: What is the set keyed on?

choices.text: Refused, because the shop was full
choices.why: The limit is per source, not per shop.

choices.text: Opened: branch has a count of its own
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Refused, because branch is on the same segment as remote
choices.why: Counts are per address, not per segment.

choices.text: Delayed until remote closed one
choices.why: Nothing queues; it is accepted or rejected.

prompt: Why does the limit answer with reject with tcp reset instead of drop?
hint: What does the client see in each case?

choices.text: A reset uses less bandwidth than a drop
choices.why: A drop sends nothing, which is less.

choices.text: drop is not allowed inside a dynamic set rule
choices.why: It is allowed.

choices.text: A reset removes the client from the set
choices.why: Closing connections does that.

choices.text: The client learns at once instead of waiting
choices.why: Right: Connection refused.

prompt: Why does a per-source connection limit do nothing against a distributed attack?
hint: How many connections does each source open?

choices.text: Distributed attacks use UDP
choices.why: Some do; the reason is the count.

choices.text: Each of many sources stays under it
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The dynamic set fills after 65535 sources
choices.why: Even far fewer sources defeat it.

choices.text: The firewall cannot count connections from the internet
choices.why: It counted remote's.

prompt: A browser opens up to ___ connections to one host, so a per-source limit of four would refuse ordinary visitors.
A 60-byte question produces a 3,000-byte answer. What is the amplification factor?

choices.why: Off by a factor of ten.
Right.
That is the answer's size.
That is the difference, not the ratio.

prompt: Which measures keep your network from being part of a reflection attack? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A public DNS server that refuses names it is not responsible for
choices.why: It cannot be used as a reflector.

choices.text: Refusing to send packets whose source address is not yours
choices.why: The forged questions never leave.

choices.text: SYN cookies on the web server
choices.why: That protects the server from a SYN flood.

choices.text: A per-source connection limit on the shop
choices.why: That limits clients of the shop.

prompt: The lab's DNS server answered REFUSED for example.org. What does that show?
hint: Whose names does it answer for?

choices.text: It is down
choices.why: It answered, and for www it said NOERROR.

choices.text: example.org does not exist in DNS
choices.why: That would be NXDOMAIN from a resolver.

choices.text: It is not an open resolver
choices.why: Right: no-resolv.

choices.text: The firewall blocked the question
choices.why: The server itself answered.

prompt: Match each upstream measure to how it works.

pairs.right: traffic routed through a provider that absorbs floods
the public address spread over many locations
one address announced from many places

prompt: conntrack -S shows drop and early_drop climbing. What is happening?
hint: Those two count what the table could not keep.

choices.text: The table is full and connections are refused or evicted
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The firewall's rules are dropping more packets
choices.why: Rule drops are not these counters.

choices.text: Connections are closing normally
choices.why: Normal closes do not count here.

choices.text: The ICMP rate limit is being reached
choices.why: Unrelated counter.

prompt: When is the decision to buy a scrubbing service made well?
hint: It has to be arranged before.

choices.text: During the first attack, when its cost is clear
choices.why: Too late to route traffic through it.

choices.text: Beforehand, from what an hour down costs
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: After the firewall has been upgraded
choices.why: A bigger firewall does not widen the link.

choices.text: Never, since SYN cookies make it unnecessary
choices.why: Cookies do nothing for a full link.

prompt: Order where a flood meets defences on its way in, from first to last.
items: the firewall's per-source limits and connection table
trap: Each layer sees what the one before it let through.

prompt: The shop slows to a crawl. conntrack -C on fw is near its maximum and the link is half used. Which kind of attack does this point to?

choices.text: Volumetric
choices.why: The link is only half used.

choices.text: Protocol
choices.why: Right: a table is filling.

choices.text: Application
choices.why: That would show in the proxy and the application first.

choices.text: Reflection from the company's DNS
choices.why: It refuses foreign names.

prompt: An office of 200 people reaches the shop through one NAT address. What should the per-source limit be based on?

choices.text: Four, as in the lesson
choices.why: Four was a demonstration.

choices.text: One connection per person
choices.why: Browsers open several.

choices.text: The busiest legitimate source measured, with margin
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: No limit, since NAT makes limits useless
choices.why: It changes the number, not the usefulness.
